en.name: Urban V
en.summary: A monk-pope who briefly returned the papacy to Rome before renewed Italian instability drove him back to Avignon, where he died soon after.
en.body: Urban V, a Benedictine monk chosen while not even a cardinal, achieved what several predecessors had considered: he moved the papal court back to Rome in 1367, ending, if only temporarily, decades of Avignon residence. Continued unrest in Italy and pressure from the French cardinals led him to return to Avignon in 1370, where he died within weeks — a decision later regarded by contemporaries, including Catherine of Siena, as a tragic reversal of the return to Rome.
